hero.eyebrow: Fixed scope, fixed price, in CAD
hero.headline: You have the offer. You do not have a page that takes money.
hero.sub: One page, written and built around what you actually sell, with your own checkout link on it. Live on a real URL within 48 hours of the brief. CAD 300, flat.
hero.note: You see the finished page working on a live URL before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: What lands in your hands
sections.intro: Everything below is inside the flat price. Nothing here is an upsell.

items.title: Copy written for your offer
items.body: Headline, the offer, what is included, objection handling, and a close. The copy is written from your brief, not dropped into a placeholder theme.

items.title: Your checkout, not ours
items.body: Your Stripe, Square, Ko-fi, PayPal or booking link goes on the button. Our payment account never touches your page — the money moves from your customer to you.

items.title: Privacy and terms pages
items.body: Written to match what the page actually does, with a real last-updated date. Most one-page sites ship without these and quietly need them.

items.title: No cookie banner
items.body: Static files, no analytics, no advertising, no third-party script or font. Nothing to consent to, so nothing to interrupt the visitor with.

items.title: Fast by construction
items.body: One HTML file with the stylesheet inlined and an SVG icon built in. No framework, no bundle, no render-blocking request to a CDN.

items.title: Real security headers
items.body: Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, nosniff, frame-deny and a locked-down Permissions-Policy, configured at the edge rather than left at defaults.

items.title: Readable in dark mode
items.body: The page follows the visitor's system theme instead of blinding half of them at night. Tested in both.

items.title: Works on a phone first
items.body: Built narrow and scaled up, with real tap targets and no horizontal scroll at 320 pixels wide.

items.title: The files are yours
items.body: On payment you get the source and the deploy configuration. You can hand it to anyone later. Nothing is locked to us.

sections.heading: Four steps, two days
sections.intro: No discovery call, no proposal deck, no scope negotiation. The scope is fixed before you start, which is why the price can be.

items.title: You send the brief
items.body: What you sell, who buys it, the price, and where the money should go. A few paragraphs by email is enough. No form to fill in.

items.title: We build it
items.body: Copy written, page built, privacy and terms generated, checkout wired to your link, deployed. You get a live URL you can open on your phone.

items.title: One round of changes
items.body: You read it and send corrections in one message. Wording, prices, order of sections, the accent colour. Turned around same day.

items.title: You pay, then it is yours
items.body: Interac e-Transfer, CAD 300. Then the page points at your domain if you have one, and the source and deploy config come to you.

sections.heading: One number, in Canadian dollars
sections.intro: A one-page site in Canada is commonly quoted between CAD 500 and CAD 3,000, and a freelancer build of a small-business site runs CAD 1,500 to CAD 5,000. This is cheaper than any of that for one reason: the scope is fixed and narrow, so there is nothing to estimate.

sections.heading: What this is not
sections.intro: Said up front, because a fixed price only works if both sides know where it stops.

items.title: Not a brand identity
items.body: Your existing logo is used if you have one. If you do not, the page runs on clean type and a monogram, which looks deliberate rather than unfinished.

items.title: Not a photo shoot
items.body: Your photos are used. No stock imagery is bought or invented, and no image of a person who did not agree to appear goes on your page.

items.title: Not a full storefront
items.body: One offer, or a small handful, each pointing at your own checkout. A hundred-product storefront with inventory needs different tooling and an honest quote.

items.title: Not an app or database
items.body: The page links out to whatever tool you already use for that. Building one is a different project.

items.title: Not ongoing edits
items.body: One round of changes is included. After handover you hold the source, and further work is quoted separately or done by anyone you like.

items.title: Not professional advice
items.body: The privacy and terms pages are plain-language descriptions of what your site does. If your situation needs a professional opinion, get one — we will say so rather than guess.

sections.heading: The ones that actually get asked

items.q: Why would you take CAD 300 for this?
items.a: Because the build is fixed-scope and genuinely fast, and because the hosting costs nothing. There is no agency overhead in the number, no account manager and no monthly retainer behind it. The trade you are making is scope: you get one excellent page, not a bespoke multi-page project. If you need the multi-page project, the CAD 500 to CAD 3,000 one-page quotes and the CAD 1,500 to CAD 5,000 freelancer site builds are the honest comparison, and I am not competing with them.

items.q: Do I pay before or after?
items.a:
After. You get a live URL, you open it, you read it, you send corrections. You pay when it is right. That removes the awkward part of hiring a stranger on the internet.
Until payment the page sits on our subdomain. On payment it points at your domain and the source comes to you.

items.q: What does hosting cost me afterwards?
items.a:
Nothing, on the free tier it is deployed to. Cloudflare's free plan permits commercial use and does not charge for bandwidth on static files, which is the entire reason this page can be hosted at no cost without breaking anyone's terms.
A domain name is separate and costs roughly CAD 12 to CAD 22 a year depending on the registrar, paid to them, not to us. You do not need one to go live.

items.q: Can I edit it myself later?
items.a: Yes. It is plain HTML and CSS with no build step required to read it, plus a small generator if you want to regenerate the page from a JSON file. Anyone who writes HTML can change it. You are not locked into a proprietary editor.

items.q: Whose payment account is on the page?
items.a: Yours, always. A link to your Stripe, Square, Ko-fi, PayPal, Calendly or whatever you already use. Our payment details never appear on your page and we never sit between you and your customer's money.

items.q: What if I do not like it?
items.a: Send the corrections in one message and they get made. If you look at the result and decide you do not want it at all, you do not pay and nothing was ever live under your name. That is the point of paying on go-live.

items.q: Do you charge GST or HST?
items.a: Not currently. Under the Canada Revenue Agency's small-supplier threshold of CAD 30,000 in revenue there is no obligation to register for or charge GST/HST, so the invoice has no tax line. If that changes, the price shown will change with it rather than a tax appearing on top.
Yes — written, not run through a translator. The Ship Two package covers the same page in English and Korean, which matters if your customers search in one language and walk in speaking the other.

items.q: Is the copy written by AI?
items.a: AI is used as part of how the page is produced, which is exactly why the price is what it is. Every line is reviewed before you see it, and if you would rather it were not used, say so in the brief and it will not be.
